findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the `bridge_state/` -> `.rebar/bridge/` move (keep-last-5/30-day retention) to CHANGELOG.md and docs/release-notes.md within S8 (e6ee), and add both files to its scope.
evidence: Parent AC6: 'Release notes and CHANGELOG record the package rename, the deleted env vars, and the `bridge_state/` move. Checked by the docs gates in `make verify`.'
e6ee Scope lists docs edits as `docs/adr/0099-...:72`, `docs/user-guide.md`, `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`, `docs/concurrency.md` — no CHANGELOG.md and no docs/release-notes.md.
bf96 records only the package rename in CHANGELOG/release-notes; fc96 records only the deleted env vars; neither records the bridge_state/ -> .rebar/bridge/ move.
e6ee BREAKING note states the move but is a ticket-description note, not a CHANGELOG/release-notes edit.
findings.finding: Parent criterion 6 requires the bridge_state/ move to be recorded in BOTH release notes and CHANGELOG, but the only sibling that moves scratch (S8, e6ee) names neither CHANGELOG.md nor docs/release-notes.md in its scope; no other sibling records the bridge_state/ move either.
scenarios: `make verify` docs gate asserts the CHANGELOG/release-notes mention the bridge_state/ move and fails because no story wrote that entry.
Operators reading release notes do not learn that `<repo>/bridge_state/` moved to `<repo>/.rebar/bridge/` and keep looking in the old location.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend e6ee's scope and approach to add a BREAKING CHANGELOG.md entry and a docs/release-notes.md note for the scratch-path move, matching how bf96 records the rename and fc96 records the env-var deletions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to S4 (cfbd) an AC running `git grep -nE 'os\.kill(pg)?\(|signal\.SIG(TERM|KILL)' -- src/rebar/reconciler src/rebar/_bridge_runner*` (expects empty) and a unit test asserting reap_process_group is called once with the child's pid on a forced timeout.
evidence: Parent AC3: '... `git grep -nE 'os\.kill(pg)?\(|signal\.SIG(TERM|KILL)' -- src/rebar/reconciler src/rebar/_bridge_runner*` prints nothing, which proves no second reaper was written.' and 'one test monkeypatches `reap_process_group` at the `_bridge_runner` import site and asserts it is called once with the child's pid on a forced timeout'.

cfbd ACs cover: no `rebar bridge` argv / no legacy_exit, grandchild reaped (check_orphaned_load.py), docs/exit-codes.md wording, make verify — but neither the os.kill/signal.SIG source grep nor a reap_process_group-called-once-with-pid assertion.
Parent 'Approach' invariant: 'a new `kill`/`killpg` call site under `src/rebar/` outside `_proc.py` is a defect in S4' — the grep is the stated proof, and it is absent from S4's ACs.
No other sibling owns _bridge_runner reaping, so this check is covered by no sibling.
findings.finding: Parent criterion 3 names two observable checks that S4 (cfbd) does not deliver in its acceptance criteria: (a) the `git grep -nE 'os\.kill(pg)?\(|signal\.SIG(TERM|KILL)' -- src/rebar/reconciler src/rebar/_bridge_runner*` that proves no second reaper was written, and (b) the test that monkeypatches reap_process_group at the _bridge_runner import site and asserts it is called once with the child's pid on a forced timeout.
scenarios: S4 reimplements signalling inline (a second reaper) instead of calling rebar._proc.reap_process_group; the grandchild test still passes but the no-second-reaper invariant is violated and goes undetected because the proving grep is not an AC.
The reap-called-once-with-pid behavioural guarantee is not pinned, so a regression that reaps the wrong pid or twice is not caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Promote the parent's two named checks into cfbd's acceptance criteria and testing section so the no-second-reaper grep and the reap-called-once-with-pid assertion are verified by this story.

findings.finding: The move of bridge scratch from repo-root `bridge_state/` to `.rebar/bridge/` does not state what happens to the already-accumulated `bridge_state/` directory — whether its contents are migrated, deleted, or simply abandoned — leaving a destructive/transition step partially unspecified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure-disposition contract for run_guarded_pass lease contention: what a bridge_sync (and CLI/library) caller surfaces when the reconciler lease is already held — e.g. a retryable/transient 'pass in progress' rather than a fatal error.
evidence: Plan: 'the library's _lib_ops._bridge_run bypasses the guarded core so an MCP bridge_sync runs an unlocked live pass (a bug)'
Plan: all three entry points now 'run a live pass through one guarded core (run_guarded_pass) that takes the reconciler lease'
ABSENCE: no disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) is stated for a bridge_sync that cannot acquire the already-held lease
findings.finding: S3 routes the MCP bridge_sync tool (previously bypassing the guarded core via _lib_ops._bridge_run) through run_guarded_pass, which 'takes the reconciler lease' — but the plan never states the disposition surfaced to the caller when that lease is already held (a concurrent pass running). Lease contention is a newly-reachable failure arm for bridge_sync created by this bug fix.
findings.location: Context/Problem + S3; AC line 2 ('all run a live pass through one guarded core (run_guarded_pass) that takes the reconciler lease')
scenarios: An operator triggers MCP bridge_sync while a CLI or scheduled guarded pass already holds the reconciler lease

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In S7, state whether the ~20 live `_call_with_retry` call sites (dispatch_one/apply_inbound/apply_inbound_events/apply_outbound) are already covered by the ADR-0103 coordinator RetryBudget or must be migrated to it, and make the independent-confirmation gate prove no live call site loses retry before deletion.
evidence: The active wrapper `dispatch_apply_phases._call_with_retry` (dispatch_apply_phases.py:76) is invoked at ~20 live call sites across dispatch_one.py, apply_inbound.py, apply_inbound_events.py and apply_outbound.py (create_issue/update_issue/add_label/set_entity_property/set_parent/delete_issue/delete_issue_link).

ADR 0103 introduced a coordinator-owned `RetryBudget` (coordinator.py:48, retry_budget.py:104) as the intended retry owner; the plan frames `_call_with_retry` as leftover that 'survives past ADR 0103 S3'.

A pure deletion of the function/tests (AC4: '_call_with_retry ... deleted with their tests') without migrating or confirming each call site either loses retry on idempotent Jira writes or fails to compile.
findings.finding: S7 'retire _call_with_retry' treats a live, heavily-used per-call retry wrapper as dead code without specifying how its ~20 call sites preserve retry behavior.
findings.location: Child decomposition S7; Acceptance Criteria bullet 4; Context 'and _call_with_retry survives past ADR 0103 S3'
scenarios: S7 deletes the function but call sites in dispatch_one/apply_inbound still reference it -> import/NameError or silently dropped retry on 429/5xx writes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In S8, enumerate every repo-root bridge_state/ artifact to repoint under .rebar/bridge/ (snapshots/, mapping.json, sync-log-*.jsonl, bridge_alerts/, comment_id_divergence.json) and explicitly exclude the committed tracker-dir `.bridge_state/` so the two paths are not conflated.
evidence: Two distinct paths exist: committed `<tracker>/.bridge_state/` (bindings.json, projects.json, peer_confirmations.json, impossible_links.json — merge=ours on the tickets branch) vs. repo-root scratch `bridge_state/` (snapshots/, mapping.json, sync-log-*.jsonl, bridge_alerts/, comment_id_divergence.json).

Repo-root bridge_state/ is read/written in applier.py:560/669, load_phase.py:180/200, fetcher.py:629, apply_planning.py:341, dispatch_one.py:165, apply_inbound.py:107, apply_handlers.py:598, alert_store.py:23, invariants.py:404.

The plan's single AC line ('Bridge scratch lives under .rebar/bridge/') does not list these sites or exclude the committed `.bridge_state/`; an incomplete repoint leaves scratch split across two roots and breaks keep-last-5 pruning.
findings.finding: Criterion 5 / S8 moves 'bridge scratch' to .rebar/bridge/ without enumerating the repo-root bridge_state/ reader-writer sites that must repoint, nor disambiguating from the committed .bridge_state/ tracker-dir path that must NOT move.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 5; Child decomposition S8; Context 'bridge_state/ accumulates at the repo root with no retention'
scenarios: S8 repoints snapshots/ and sync-logs but misses mapping.json (dispatch_one/apply_inbound/apply_handlers) or comment_id_divergence.json (invariants) -> split scratch; retention prunes only part.
A developer mistakes the committed `.bridge_state/` for scratch and moves it, breaking the tickets-branch merge=ours bindings residency.
